units.zh: 裴讓之 弟諏之 讞之 皇甫和 李構 張宴之 陸卬 王松年 劉禕
units.en: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi
units.literal: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi

units.zh: 裴讓之，字士禮。
units.en: Pei Rangzhi, styled Shili.
units.literal: Pei Rangzhi, styled Shili.

units.zh: 年十六喪父，殆不勝哀，其母辛氏泣撫之曰：「棄我滅性，得為孝子乎？」
units.en: At sixteen he lost his father, grief nearly more than he could bear; his mother Lady Xin wept as she comforted him, saying, "Would you abandon me and destroy yourself—could that make you a filial son?"
units.literal: At age sixteen he lost his father, grief nearly beyond bearing; his mother the Lady Xin wept as she comforted him, saying, "Would you abandon me and destroy your nature—could that make you a filial son?"

units.zh: 由是自勉。
units.en: Thereupon he forced himself to recover.
units.literal: Thereupon he urged himself on.

units.zh: 辛氏高明婦則，又閑禮度。
units.en: Lady Xin was an exemplary woman of high principle and also well versed in ritual.
units.literal: Lady Xin was a lofty and clear exemplar among women, and also versed in ritual propriety.

units.zh: 夫喪，諸子多幼弱，廣延師友，或親自教授。
units.en: After her husband's death the sons were still young; she brought in many tutors or taught them herself.
units.literal: When her husband died, the sons were mostly young and weak; she widely invited teachers and friends, or personally instructed them.

units.zh: 內外親屬有吉凶禮制，多取則焉。
units.en: Relatives near and far took her as their model for ritual on happy and mournful occasions.
units.literal: Kin within and without, for auspicious or inauspicious occasions and ritual rules, mostly took her as their model.

units.zh: 讓之少好學，有文俊辯，早得聲譽。
units.en: Rangzhi loved learning from youth; gifted in letters and sharp in debate, he won an early reputation.
units.literal: Rangzhi from youth loved learning, had literary talent, sharp eloquence, and early won reputation.

units.zh: 魏天平中舉秀才，對策高第。
units.en: Under Wei in the Tianping era he was recommended as xiucai and ranked first in the policy examination.
units.literal: In Wei times under Tianping he was recommended as xiucai; in policy responses he ranked at the top.

units.zh: 累遷屯田主客郎中，省中語曰：「能賦詩，裴讓之。」
units.en: He rose to director of agriculture and master of guests in the masters of writing; at court they said, "Who can write poetry? Pei Rangzhi."
units.literal: He rose repeatedly to Director of Agriculture and Master of Guests in the Masters of Writing; within the ministry they said, "Who can compose poetry? Pei Rangzhi."

units.zh: 為太原公開府記室。
units.en: He became recorder on the staff of the Prince of Taiyuan.
units.literal: He served as recorder for the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment.

units.zh: 與楊愔友善，相遇則清談竟日。
units.en: He was close to Yang Yin; whenever they met they talked the day away.
units.literal: He was friendly with Yang Yin; when they met they held pure talk the whole day.

units.zh: 愔每云：「此人風流警拔，裴文季為不亡矣。」
units.en: Yin often said, "This man's spirit is striking and outstanding—Pei Wenji lives on in him."
units.literal: Yin would often say, "This man's spirit is alert and outstanding—Pei Wenji is not dead after all."

units.zh: 梁使至，帝令讓之攝主客郎。
units.en: When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi serve as acting master of guests.
units.literal: When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi act as master of guests attendant.

units.zh: 第二弟諏之奔關右，兄弟五人皆拘繫。
units.en: His second brother Souzhi fled to the western passes; all five brothers were imprisoned.
units.literal: His second younger brother Souzhi fled to Guanxi; all five brothers were detained.

units.zh: 神武問曰：「諏之何在？」
units.en: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?"
units.literal: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?"

units.zh: 答曰：「昔吳、蜀二國，諸葛兄弟各得遂心，況讓之老母在，君臣分定，失忠與孝，愚夫不為。
units.en: He answered, "Long ago Wu and Shu were two realms, yet the Zhuge brothers each got his way; all the more when Rangzhi's aged mother is here—lord and subject each have his place; to lose loyalty and filial piety together is what no fool would choose.
units.literal: He answered, "In former times Wu and Shu were two states, yet the Zhuge brothers each had his wish fulfilled; how much more when Rangzhi's old mother is here—ruler and minister roles are fixed; to lose both loyalty and filial piety is what a fool would not do.

units.zh: 伏願明公以誠信待物，若以不信處物，物亦安能自信？
units.en: I beg you, my lord, to meet the world with sincerity; if you meet the world without trust, how can the world trust you in return?
units.literal: I humbly wish the lord will treat things with sincerity and trust; if you treat things without trust, how can things in turn trust you?

units.zh: 以此定霸，猶卻行而求道耳。」
units.en: To found dominion on that is like walking backward to find the road."
units.literal: To settle hegemony on this basis is like walking backward to seek the Way."

units.zh: 神武善其言，兄弟俱釋。
units.en: Gao Huan approved his reply, and the brothers were all freed.
units.literal: Gao Huan approved his words, and the brothers were all released.

units.zh: 歷文襄大將軍主簿，兼中書舍人，後兼散騎常侍，聘梁。
units.en: He served as chief clerk on Gao Cheng's staff as grand general, then as concurrent secretariat attendant and later as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on a mission to Liang.
units.literal: He served successively as chief clerk to Gao Cheng as grand general, concurrently secretariat attendant, later concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and as envoy to Liang.

units.zh: 文襄嘗入朝，讓之導引，容儀蘊藉，文襄目之曰：「士禮佳舍人。」
units.en: Once when Gao Cheng went to court Rangzhi led him in with composed, refined bearing; Gao Cheng glanced at him and said, "Shili is a fine gentleman of the secretariat."
units.literal: Gao Cheng once entered court; Rangzhi guided him in; his bearing was composed and refined; Gao Cheng looked at him and said, "Shili is a fine attendant."

units.zh: 遷長兼中書侍郎，領舍人。
units.en: He was promoted to senior concurrent secretariat vice director while retaining his attendant post.
units.literal: He was transferred to senior concurrent secretariat vice director, still holding attendant.

units.zh: 齊受禪，靜帝遜居別宮，與諸臣別，讓之流涕歔欷。
units.en: When Qi took the throne, Emperor Jing retired to a side palace to bid the ministers farewell; Rangzhi wept aloud.
units.literal: When Qi received the mandate, Emperor Jing withdrew to a separate palace to take leave of the ministers; Rangzhi wept and sobbed.

units.zh: 以參掌儀注，封寧都縣男。
units.en: For helping draft ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as baron of Ningdu county.
units.literal: For helping manage ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningdu.

units.zh: 帝欲以為黃門郎，或言其體重，不堪趨侍，乃除清河太守。
units.en: The emperor wished to appoint him yellow gate attendant, but some said he was too heavyset for palace attendance, so he was made grand administrator of Qinghe instead.
units.literal: The emperor wished to make him yellow gate attendant; some said his body was too heavy and he could not bear hurrying in attendance, so he was instead made grand administrator of Qinghe.

units.zh: 至郡未幾，楊愔謂讓之諸弟曰：「我與賢兄交款，企聞善政。
units.en: Soon after he took office in the commandery, Yang Yin told Rangzhi's brothers, "Your elder brother and I are close; I have been eager to hear of his good rule.
units.literal: Not long after he reached the commandery, Yang Yin said to Rangzhi's younger brothers, "Your worthy elder brother and I are close in friendship; I look forward to hearing of good government.

units.zh: 適有人從清河來，云姦吏斂跡，盜賊清靖。
units.en: Someone has just arrived from Qinghe saying corrupt officials have pulled back and robbers are subdued.
units.literal: Just now someone came from Qinghe and said corrupt clerks have drawn in their claws and bandits are quiet.

units.zh: 期月之期，翻然更速。」
units.en: What should have taken a month has come about even sooner."
units.literal: The target of a full month has been overturned still faster."

units.zh: 清河有二豪吏田轉貴、孫舍興久吏姦猾，多有侵削，因事遂脅人取財。
units.en: Qinghe had two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuanggui and Sun Shexing—veteran, cunning officials who often skimmed funds and used any pretext to extort money.
units.literal: In Qinghe were two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuangui and Sun Shexing—long-serving, crafty and slippery, who often shaved off shares and, using incidents, then extorted people's wealth.

units.zh: 計贓依律不至死。
units.en: By law the amount of stolen goods did not warrant death.
units.literal: Calculating the booty by law did not reach death.

units.zh: 讓之以其亂法，殺之。
units.en: Rangzhi executed them for subverting the law.
units.literal: Rangzhi, because they had disrupted the law, killed them.

units.zh: 時清河王岳為司州牧，遣部從事案之。
units.en: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was governor of Si province and sent a staff investigator to review the case.
units.literal: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was inspector of Si province; he sent a bureau aide to investigate the case.

units.zh: 侍中高德政舊與讓之不協，案奏言：「當陛下受禪之時，讓之眷戀魏朝，嗚咽流涕，比為內官，情非所願。」
units.en: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long disliked Rangzhi; in his report he wrote, "When Your Majesty took the throne, Rangzhi clung to the Wei house and wept; service at court was not what he wished."
units.literal: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long been at odds with Rangzhi; in the memorial of investigation he said, "When Your Majesty received the mandate, Rangzhi cherished the Wei court, sobbed and wept; compared with being an inner-court official, his heart was not in it."

units.zh: 旣而楊愔請救之，云：「罪不合死。」
units.en: Yang Yin then pleaded for him, saying, "The offense does not deserve death."
units.literal: Before long Yang Yin pleaded for his life, saying, "The crime does not merit death."

units.zh: 文宣大怒，謂愔曰：「欲得與裴讓之同冢耶！」
units.en: Gao Yang flew into a rage and said to Yin, "Do you want to lie in the same grave as Pei Rangzhi?"
units.literal: Gao Yang was greatly enraged and said to Yin, "Do you wish to share a tomb with Pei Rangzhi?"

units.zh: 於是無敢言者。
units.en: After that no one dared speak up.
units.literal: Thereupon none dared speak further.

units.zh: 事奏，竟賜死於家。
units.en: When the case was finalized, he was ordered to take his own life at home.
units.literal: When the matter was reported, in the end he was ordered to die at home.

units.zh: 讓之次弟諏之。
units.en: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.
units.literal: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.

units.zh: 諏之，字士正，少好儒學，釋褐太學博士。
units.en: Souzhi, styled Shizheng, loved Confucian studies from youth and on first office became an erudite of the Imperial Academy.
units.literal: Souzhi, styled Shizheng, from youth loved Confucian learning; on leaving the robe he became erudite of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 嘗從常景借書百卷，十許日便返。
units.en: Once he borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in about ten days.
units.literal: He once borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in some ten days.

units.zh: 景疑其不能讀，每卷策問，應答無遺。
units.en: Jing doubted he could have read them and quizzed him scroll by scroll; he answered without a gap.
units.literal: Jing suspected he had not read them; he questioned him on each scroll, and he answered without omission.

units.zh: 景嘆曰：「應奉五行俱下，禰衡一覽便記，今復見之於裴生矣。」
units.en: Jing sighed, "Ying Feng took in the Five Classics at a stroke and Mi Heng remembered at one glance—today the same gift appears in Master Pei."
units.literal: Jing sighed and said, "Ying Feng could take in the Five Classics at once, Mi Heng remembered on a single reading—today I see it again in Master Pei."

units.zh: 楊愔闔門改葬，托諏之頓作十餘墓誌，文皆可觀。
units.en: When Yang Yin reburied his entire clan, he had Souzhi write more than ten epitaphs in quick succession, each of them presentable.
units.literal: When Yang Yin had his whole clan reburied, he entrusted Souzhi to dash off more than ten epitaphs at once; the texts were all worth reading.

units.zh: 讓之、諏之及皇甫和弟亮並知名於洛下，時人語曰：「諏勝於讓，和不如亮。」
units.en: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He's brother Liang were all famous in Luoyang; contemporaries said, "Souzhi outdoes Rangzhi; He cannot match Liang."
units.literal: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He's younger brother Liang were all famed in Luoyang; people of the time said, "Souzhi surpasses Rangzhi; He is not the equal of Liang."

units.zh: 司空高乾致書曰：「相屈為戶曹參軍。」
units.en: Minister of works Gao Gan wrote inviting him to serve as household census aide.
units.literal: Minister of Works Gao Gan sent a letter saying, "I would bend you to serve as household census aide."

units.zh: 諏之復書不受署。
units.en: Souzhi answered by letter and declined the post.
units.literal: Souzhi replied by letter and would not accept appointment.

units.zh: 沛王開大司馬府，辟為記室。
units.en: When Prince Kai of Pei opened his grand marshal's office, Souzhi was recruited as recorder.
units.literal: When Prince Kai of Pei opened his grand marshal's office, Souzhi was summoned as recorder.

units.zh: 遷鄴後，諏之留在河南，西魏領軍獨孤信入據金墉，以諏之為開府屬，號曰「洛陽遺彥。」
units.en: After the court moved to Ye, Souzhi stayed in Henan; Western Wei's commanding general Dugu Xin seized Jinyong, appointed Souzhi to his staff, and called him "the last eminent man of Luoyang."
units.literal: After the move to Ye, Souzhi remained in Henan; Western Wei commanding general Dugu Xin entered and seized Jinyong, made Souzhi staff officer of his office, and styled him "the surviving worthy of Luoyang."

units.zh: 信敗，諏之居南山，洛州刺史王元軌召為中從事。
units.en: After Xin was defeated, Souzhi dwelt on South Mountain; Luoyang inspector Wang Yuangui appointed him central aide.
units.literal: When Xin was defeated, Souzhi lived on South Mountain; Luoyang inspector Wang Yuangui summoned him as central aide.

units.zh: 西師忽至，尋退，遂隨西師入關。
units.en: Western troops came suddenly and soon withdrew; he then followed the western army through the passes into Guanzhong.
units.literal: Western troops suddenly arrived, then soon withdrew; he thereupon followed the western army into the passes.

units.zh: 周文帝以為大行臺倉曹郎中，卒。
units.en: Prince Wen of Zhou appointed him director of granaries on the grand mobile staff; he died in that post.
units.literal: Prince Wen of Zhou made him director of granaries on the Grand Mobile Staff; he died in office.

units.zh: 贈徐州刺史。
units.en: He was posthumously made inspector of Xu province.
units.literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Xu province.

units.zh: 讞之，字士平，七歲便勤學，早知名。
units.en: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, was studying hard by age seven and was known early.
units.literal: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, at seven sui was already diligent in study and early won fame.

units.zh: 累遷司徒主簿。
units.en: He rose to chief clerk in the ministry of education.
units.literal: He rose repeatedly to chief clerk of the Ministry of Education.

units.zh: 楊愔每稱嘆云：「河東士族，京官不少，唯此家兄弟，全無鄉音。」
units.en: Yang Yin often praised him, saying, "Hedong has many families with capital officials, but only these brothers speak without a hometown accent."
units.literal: Yang Yin would often praise him, saying, "Among the gentry clans of Hedong there are many capital officials, but only this household's brothers have no trace of home accent."

units.zh: 讞之雖年少，不妄交遊，唯與隴西辛術、趙郡李繪、頓丘李構、清河崔瞻為忘年之友。
units.en: Though still young, Yanzhi did not socialize lightly; only Xin Shu of Longxi, Li Hui of Zhao commandery, Li Gou of Dunqiu, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe were his friends despite the age gap.
units.literal: Though Yanzhi was still young, he did not make friends lightly; only Longxi Xin Shu, Zhao commandery Li Hui, Dunqiu Li Gou, and Qinghe Cui Zhan were his friends across the years.

units.zh: 昭帝梓宮將還鄴，轉儀曹郎，尤悉歷代故事、儀註，喪禮皆能裁正。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was to return to Ye, he was made gentleman of the rituals bureau; he knew dynastic precedent and ceremonial law especially well and could set right every mourning rite.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was about to return to Ye, he was transferred to gentleman of the rituals bureau; he especially knew past dynasties' precedents and ritual regulations, and could correct all mourning rites.

units.zh: 為永昌太守，客旅過郡，出私財供給，人間無所，預代下出，為吏人所懷。
units.en: As grand administrator of Yongchang, he paid traveling guests from his own purse when the commandery had nothing on hand, advancing funds for them in advance, and officials and commoners alike were grateful.
units.literal: As grand administrator of Yongchang, when travelers passed through the commandery he supplied them from private funds; where the district had nothing, he advanced payment on their behalf, and the clerks and people were grateful.

units.zh: 齊亡仕周，卒伊川太守。
units.en: After Qi fell he served Zhou and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.
units.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou's service and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.

units.zh: 皇甫和，字長諧，安定朝那人，其先因官寓居漢中。
units.en: Huangfu He, styled Changxie, was from Chaona in Anding; his forebears had settled in Hanzhong through official postings.
units.literal: Huangfu He, styled Changxie, was a man of Chaona in Anding; his ancestors because of office had taken residence in Hanzhong.

units.zh: 祖澄，南齊秦、梁二州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Cheng had been inspector of Qin and Liang under Southern Qi.
units.literal: His grandfather Cheng was inspector of Qin and Liang in Southern Qi.

units.zh: 父徽，字子玄，梁安定、略陽二郡守。
units.en: His father Hui, styled Zixuan, had been grand administrator of Anding and Lüeyang in Liang.
units.literal: His father Hui, styled Zixuan, was grand administrator of Anding and Lüeyang in Liang.

units.zh: 魏正始二年，隨其妻父夏侯道遷入魏，道遷別上勳書，欲以徽為元謀。
units.en: In Wei, second year of Zhengshi, he followed his wife's father Xiahou Daoqian into Wei service; Daoqian filed a separate merit roll naming Hui as chief plotter.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi in Wei, he followed his wife's father Xiahou Daoqian in entering Wei; Daoqian separately submitted a merit roster wishing to list Hui as chief conspirator.

units.zh: 徽曰：「創謀之始，本不關預，雖貪榮賞，內愧於心。」
units.en: Hui said, "I took no part when the plot began; though I crave honor and reward, my conscience would not bear it."
units.literal: Hui said, "At the beginning of the plot I had no part in it; though I covet glory and reward, inwardly I am ashamed."

units.zh: 遂拒而不許。
units.en: He refused and would not accept.
units.literal: He therefore refused and would not accept.

units.zh: 梁州刺史羊靈祐重其敦實，表為征虜府司馬，卒。
units.en: Liang inspector Yang Lingyou respected his solid character and recommended him as staff officer on the campaign against barbarians; he died in that post.
units.literal: Liang inspector Yang Lingyou valued his honesty and substance and memorialized him as staff officer of the campaign against barbarians; he died in office.

units.zh: 和十一而孤，母夏侯氏，才明有禮則，親授以經書。
units.en: He was orphaned at eleven; his mother Lady Xiahou was talented, principled, and versed in ritual, and taught him the classics herself.
units.literal: He at eleven was orphaned; his mother the Lady Xiahou was talented, clear, and observant of ritual propriety, and personally taught him the classics.

units.zh: 及長，深沉有雅量，尤明禮儀，宗親吉凶，多相諮訪。
units.en: As an adult he was grave and measured, especially skilled in ritual; relatives consulted him on happy and mournful occasions.
units.literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, with refined capacity, especially clear in ritual propriety; kin far and near on auspicious or inauspicious occasions mostly sought his counsel.

units.zh: 卒於濟陰太守。
units.en: He died while serving as grand administrator of Jiyin.
units.literal: He died as grand administrator of Jiyin.

units.zh: 李構，字祖基，黎陽人。
units.en: Li Gou, styled Zuji, was from Liyang.
units.literal: Li Gou, styled Zuji, was a man of Liyang.

units.zh: 祖平，魏尚書僕射。
units.en: His grandfather Ping had been vice director of the masters of writing under Wei.
units.literal: His grandfather Ping was vice director of the masters of writing in Wei.

units.zh: 構少以方正見稱，釋褐開府參軍，累遷譙州刺史，卒。
units.en: Gou was known from youth for rectitude; on first appointment he joined an opening office staff, rose to inspector of Qiao, and died there.
units.literal: Gou from youth was praised for uprightness; on leaving the robe he became staff officer of an opening office, rose repeatedly to inspector of Qiao, and died in office.

units.zh: 構從父弟庶，魏大司農諧子。
units.en: Gou's younger cousin on the father's side was Shu, son of Wei grand minister of agriculture Xie.
units.literal: Gou's younger cousin by the father's line was Shu; in Wei he was son of the grand minister of agriculture Xie.

units.zh: 方雅好學，風流規檢，甚有家風。
units.en: Refined and fond of learning, he kept strict standards of conduct and upheld the family reputation.
units.literal: Correct and elegant, he loved learning, had refined standards of conduct, and bore a strong family style.

units.zh: 稍遷臨漳令。
units.en: He was promoted step by step to magistrate of Linzhang.
units.literal: He rose gradually to magistrate of Linzhang.

units.zh: 《魏書》出，庶與盧斐、王松年等訟其不平，並繫獄。
units.en: When the History of Wei was published, Shu joined Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others in suing over its bias and was imprisoned with them.
units.literal: When the History of Wei appeared, Shu together with Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others sued over its unfairness and were all imprisoned.

units.zh: 魏收書王慧龍自云太原人，又言王瓊不善事；
units.en: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong claimed to be from Taiyuan and also said Wang Qiong was inept in his duties;
units.literal: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong called himself a man of Taiyuan, and also said Wang Qiong was poor at serving;

units.zh: 盧同附《盧玄傳》；
units.en: Lu Tong was tucked into the biography of Lu Xuan;
units.literal: Lu Tong was attached to the biography of Lu Xuan;

units.zh: 李平為陳留人，云其家貧賤。
units.en: Li Ping was called a man of Chenliu and described as coming from a poor, humble house.
units.literal: Li Ping was made a man of Chenliu, saying his family was poor and base.

units.zh: 故裴等致訟，語楊愔云：「魏收合誅。」
units.en: Hence the Pei party and others brought suit, telling Yang Yin, "Wei Shou deserves execution."
units.literal: Therefore the Pei clan and others brought the suit, saying to Yang Yin, "Wei Shou ought to be put to death."

units.zh: 愔黨助魏收，遂白顯祖罪斐等，並髡頭，鞭二百。
units.en: Yin took Wei Shou's side; they then denounced Fei and the rest to Gao Yang, and all were shaved and flogged two hundred strokes.
units.literal: Yin sided with Wei Shou; they thereupon reported to Gao Yang that Fei and the others were guilty, and all were shaved and given two hundred lashes.

units.zh: 庶死於臨漳獄中，庶兄岳痛之，終身不歷臨漳縣門。
units.en: Shu died in Linzhang jail; his elder brother Yue mourned him so deeply that he never again went through Linzhang's gate while he lived.
units.literal: Shu died in Linzhang prison; Shu's elder brother Yue grieved for him and to the end of his life never passed Linzhang's county gate.

units.zh: 張宴之，字熙德。
units.en: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.
units.literal: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.

units.zh: 幼孤有至性，為母鄭氏教誨，動依禮典。
units.en: Orphaned young, he was deeply dutiful; his mother Lady Zheng raised him by the rites, and he followed them in everything.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he had utmost nature; his mother the Lady Zheng taught and admonished him, and in action he always followed the ritual canon.

units.zh: 從尒朱榮平元顥，賜爵武成子，累遷尚書二千石郎中。
units.en: He followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao, was enfeoffed baron of Wucheng, and rose to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.
units.literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in pacifying Yuan Hao, was given the enfeoffment Baron of Wucheng, and rose repeatedly to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.

units.zh: 高岳征潁川，復以為都督中兵參軍兼記室。
units.en: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again appointed Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.
units.literal: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again made Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.

units.zh: 宴之文士，兼有武幹，每與岳帷帳之謀，又常以短兵接刃，親獲首級，深為岳所嗟賞。
units.en: Yanzhi was a literatus with martial skill; he often joined Yue's council in the tent and just as often fought hand to hand with a short blade, taking heads himself—much to Yue's admiration.
units.literal: Yanzhi was a man of letters who also had martial ability; he often joined Yue in planning within the curtains, and also often took short weapons to clash at close quarters, personally taking heads—deeply admired by Yue.

units.zh: 天保初，文宣為高陽王納宴之女為妃，令赴晉陽成禮。
units.en: At the start of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang married Yanzhi's daughter and ordered him to Jinyang to finish the wedding.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang took Yanzhi's daughter as consort and ordered Yanzhi to go to Jinyang to complete the rites.

units.zh: 宴之後園陪宴，坐客皆賦詩。
units.en: Later, at a feast in the rear garden, every guest was asked to compose a poem.
units.literal: Afterward in the rear garden he attended a feast; seated guests all composed poetry.

units.zh: 宴之詩云：「天下有道，主明臣直，雖休勿休，永貽世則。」
units.en: Yanzhi's poem ran, "When the Way holds the realm, the ruler is bright and his ministers straight; though all is calm, do not grow calm—leave the age a lasting model."
units.literal: Yanzhi's poem said, "When the realm has the Way, the lord is bright and ministers upright; though there is rest, do not rest—forever leave a model to the age."

units.zh: 文宣笑曰：「得卿箴諷，深以慰懷。」
units.en: Gao Yang laughed and said, "Your verse of counsel comforts me deeply."
units.literal: Gao Yang laughed and said, "To gain your admonition in verse deeply comforts my heart."

units.zh: 後行北徐州事，尋卽真，為吏人所愛。
units.en: He later administered North Xu province, soon received the regular appointment, and was beloved by officials and people.
units.literal: Later he acted for North Xu province and soon received the full appointment; officials and people loved him.

units.zh: 御史崔子武督察州郡，至北徐州，無所案劾，唯得百姓所制《清德頌》數篇。
units.en: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected provinces and commanderies; at North Xu he found no charges to bring, only several "Hymns of Pure Virtue" written by the people.
units.literal: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected the provinces and commanderies; reaching North Xu he found nothing to impeach, only several pieces of "Pure Virtue Praise" composed by the common people.

units.zh: 乃歎曰：「本求罪狀，遂聞頌聲。」
units.en: He sighed, "I came looking for offenses and instead heard praise."
units.literal: He thereupon sighed and said, "I came seeking crimes and instead heard songs of praise."

units.zh: 遷兗州刺史，未拜，卒。
units.en: He was transferred to inspector of Yan but died before assuming the post.
units.literal: He was transferred to inspector of Yan province; before he could take up the post he died.

units.zh: 贈齊州刺史。
units.en: He was posthumously made inspector of Qi province.
units.literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Qi province.

units.zh: 陸卬，字雲駒。
units.en: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.
units.literal: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.

units.zh: 少機悟，美風神，好學不倦，博覽群書，五經多通大義。
units.en: From youth he was quick and perceptive, handsome in spirit and bearing; he studied tirelessly, read widely, and grasped the main sense of the Five Classics.
units.literal: From youth he was quick and perceptive, of fine spirit and bearing; he loved learning without tiring, broadly reading many books, and mostly penetrated the great meaning of the Five Classics.

units.zh: 善屬文，甚為河間邢卲所賞。
units.en: Skilled in writing, he was greatly admired by Xing Shao of Hejian.
units.literal: Skilled at composing literature, he was greatly prized by Xing Shao of Hejian.

units.zh: 卲又與卬父子彰交遊，嘗謂子彰曰：「吾以卿老蚌，遂出明珠，意欲為羣拜紀可乎？」
units.en: Xing Shao also associated with Ang and his father Zizhang. He once said to Zizhang, "I take you as the old clam that bore the pearl—shall I have the company all bow in homage?"
units.literal: Shao also associated with Ang and his father Zizhang in friendship. He once said to Zizhang, "I take you as the old clam that bore the pearl—do you wish the assembly all to bow in homage?"

units.zh: 由是名譽日高，儒雅搢紳，尤所推許。
units.en: From this his reputation rose day by day; cultivated officials especially praised him.
units.literal: Thereupon his reputation rose daily; the refined scholar-gentry especially praised and upheld him.

units.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎，歷文襄大將軍主簿，中書舍人，兼中書侍郎，以本職兼太子洗馬。
units.en: He began as outer attendant of the scattered cavalry, then served as secretary to Grand General Gao Cheng, as secretariat gentleman and concurrent secretariat vice director, and in that post also as crown prince preceptor.
units.literal: He began his career as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he served as secretary to Gao Cheng, Grand General; Secretariat Gentleman; concurrently Secretariat Vice Director; and in his regular post concurrently Crown Prince Preceptor.

units.zh: 自梁、魏通和，歲有交聘，卬每兼官燕接。
units.en: Once Liang and Wei were at peace, embassies were exchanged every year; Ang repeatedly held concurrent posts to host the banquets.
units.literal: From the time Liang and Wei made peace, each year brought mutual embassies; Ang each time held a concurrent post for banquet reception.

units.zh: 在帝席賦詩，卬必先成，雖未能盡工，以敏速見美。
units.en: At imperial feasts when poems were set, Ang always finished first; though not always masterly, he was praised for his speed.
units.literal: At imperial banquets when composing verse, Ang always finished first; though his work was not fully polished, he was admired for quickness.

units.zh: 除中書侍郎，修國史。
units.en: He was made secretariat vice director and edited the national history.
units.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Vice Director and edited the national history.

units.zh: 以父憂去職，居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立。
units.en: He left office for his father's mourning and observed every rite until grief had wasted him to skin and bone.
units.literal: On his father's death he left office; in mourning he fulfilled every rite, his grief wasting him to skin and bone.

units.zh: 詔以本官起。
units.en: An edict recalled him to his former post.
units.literal: An edict recalled him to his former post.

units.zh: 文襄時鎮鄴，嘉其至行，親詣門以慰勉之。
units.en: While Gao Cheng was stationed at Ye he admired Ang's conduct, came to his door in person, and comforted him.
units.literal: When Gao Cheng held Ye, he prized Ang's utmost conduct and came in person to his gate to console and encourage him.

units.zh: 卬母魏上庸公主，初封藍田，高明婦人也，甚有志操。
units.en: Ang's mother was the Wei princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and strong moral resolve.
units.literal: Ang's mother was the Wei Princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as Princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and very strong resolve.

units.zh: 卬昆季六人，並主所生。
units.en: Ang and his brothers were six in all, all children of the same mother.
units.literal: Ang and his brothers numbered six, all born of the mistress.

units.zh: 故邢卲常謂人云：「藍田生玉，固不虛矣。」
units.en: Xing Shao often said, "Lantian breeds jade—the saying is no empty boast."
units.literal: Thus Xing Shao often told people, "Lantian breeds jade—indeed it is no empty saying."

units.zh: 主教訓諸子，皆稟義方，雖創巨痛深，出於天性，然動依禮度，亦母氏之訓焉。
units.en: Their mother trained them in the right way; though their overwhelming grief came from nature, they still acted by ritual—her teaching as well.
units.literal: The mistress instructed her sons; all received righteous training. Though their crushing grief sprang from inborn nature, in action they still followed ritual measure—also their mother's instruction.

units.zh: 卬兄弟相率廬於墓側，負土成墳，朝廷深所嗟尚，發詔褒揚，改其所居裏為孝終里。
units.en: Ang and his brothers built mourning huts beside the tomb and heaped the grave with their own hands; the court admired them deeply, issued a commendation, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong, "Filial End."
units.literal: Ang and his brothers together led huts by the tomb, carried earth to form the mound; the court deeply admired this, issued an edict of praise, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong Lane.

units.zh: 服竟當襲，不忍嗣侯。
units.en: When mourning ended he was to inherit the title, but he could not bring himself to take the marquisate.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was due to inherit, but he could not bear to succeed to the marquisate.

units.zh: 天保初，常山王薦卬器幹，文宣面授給事黃門侍郎，遷吏部郎中。
units.en: Early in Tianbao the prince of Changshan recommended Ang's ability; Gao Yang personally appointed him supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant, then made him director of the ministry of personnel.
units.literal: At the start of Tianbao, the Prince of Changshan recommended Ang's talent and capacity; Gao Yang personally appointed him Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant, then promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 上洛王思宗為清都尹，辟為邑中正，食貝丘縣幹。
units.en: When Prince of Shangluo Sizong was magistrate of Qingdu he appointed Ang head of the local selection office with the salary of Beiqiu county.
units.literal: Prince of Shangluo Sizong was magistrate of Qingdu; he summoned Ang as director of the district selection office and granted him the salary of Beiqiu county.

units.zh: 遭母喪，哀慕毀悴，殆不勝喪，至沉篤，頓昧伏枕。
units.en: At his mother's death he grieved until he was near broken by mourning; he grew critically ill, collapsed in a stupor, and could not rise from his pillow.
units.literal: On his mother's death he mourned with such grief and wasting that he nearly could not survive the mourning; he fell critically ill, collapsed in a stupor, and lay on his pillow.

units.zh: 又感風疾。
units.en: He also contracted a wind disorder.
units.literal: He also contracted a wind ailment.

units.zh: 第五弟摶遇疾臨終，謂其兄弟曰：「大兄尫病如此，性至慈愛，摶之死日，必不得使大兄知之，哭泣聲必不可聞徹，致有感慟。」
units.en: His fifth brother Tuan, on his deathbed, told the others, "The eldest brother is this ill and tender-hearted. On the day I die you must not let him know; no weeping must reach him, or it will break his heart."
units.literal: His fifth younger brother Tuan, facing illness at life's end, told his brothers, "Our eldest brother's wasting illness is like this, and his nature is deeply loving. On the day of Tuan's death you must not let the eldest brother know; sounds of weeping must not be heard reaching through, lest it stir his grief."

units.zh: 家人至於祖載，方始告之。
units.en: The family told him only when the funeral cortege departed.
units.literal: The family only told him when the funeral procession set out.

units.zh: 卬聞而悲痛，一慟便絕，年四十八。
units.en: When Ang heard, he grieved; one great sob and he was gone, at forty-eight.
units.literal: Ang heard and grieved; one great sob and he died—forty-eight years old.

units.zh: 卬自在朝，篤慎固密，不說人短，不伐己長，言論清遠，有人倫鑒裁，朝野甚悲惜之。
units.en: In office Ang was earnest and discreet; he spoke ill of no one and boasted of nothing. His speech was clear and measured, and he judged men well. Court and country mourned him deeply.
units.literal: Ang in court was earnest, cautious, and tight-lipped; he spoke no man's faults and boasted no merit of his own. His discourse was clear and far-reaching; he had discernment in human relations. Court and countryside deeply mourned him.

units.zh: 贈衛將軍、青州刺史，諡曰文。
units.en: He was posthumously made general of the guards and inspector of Qing province, with the posthumous name Wen.
units.literal: He was posthumously made General of the Guards and inspector of Qing province; his posthumous title was Wen.

units.zh: 所著文章十四卷，行於世。
units.en: His writings in fourteen scrolls circulated widely.
units.literal: His collected writings in fourteen scrolls circulated in the world.

units.zh: 齊之效廟諸歌，多卬所制。
units.en: Many of the Qi suburban-temple hymns were Ang's work.
units.literal: Many of the Qi suburban-temple songs were composed by Ang.

units.zh: 子乂嗣，襲爵始平侯。
units.en: His son Yi succeeded to the marquisate of Shiping.
units.literal: His son Yi succeeded and inherited the marquisate of Shiping.

units.zh: 王松年，少知名。
units.en: Wang Songnian was known from his youth.
units.literal: Wang Songnian was known from youth.

units.zh: 文襄臨幷州，辟為主簿，累遷通直散騎常侍，副李緯使梁。
units.en: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he made Songnian his secretary; he rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and went to Liang as deputy to Li Wei.
units.literal: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he summoned him as secretary; he rose through posts to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and served as deputy to Li Wei on an embassy to Liang.

units.zh: 還，歷位尚書郎中。
units.en: After his return he served in successive director posts in the ministry.
units.literal: On his return he held successive posts as director in the ministry.

units.zh: 魏收撰《魏書》成，松年有謗言，文宣怒，禁止之，仍加杖罰。
units.en: When Wei Shou completed the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke against it; Gao Yang was furious, had him imprisoned, and had him beaten.
units.literal: When Wei Shou finished compiling the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke slanderously of it; Gao Yang was angry, had him detained, and also had him beaten with the staff.

units.zh: 歲餘得免，除臨漳令，遷司馬、別駕、本州大中正。
units.en: After more than a year he was freed, made magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and provincial grand selection officer.
units.literal: After more than a year he was released, appointed magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and grand selection officer of his province.

units.zh: 孝昭擢拜給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: Gao Yan promoted him to supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant.
units.literal: Gao Yan promoted him to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant.

units.zh: 帝每賜坐，與論政事，甚善之。
units.en: Whenever the emperor gave him a seat and discussed affairs, he favored him greatly.
units.literal: Whenever the emperor granted him a seat and discussed state affairs with him, he was well pleased with him.

units.zh: 孝昭崩，松年馳驛至鄴都宣遺詔，發言涕泗，迄於宣罷，容色無改，辭吐諧韻。
units.en: When Gao Yan died, Songnian raced by post to Ye to proclaim the deathbed edict; he wept as he spoke, yet from beginning to end his composure did not alter and his delivery stayed measured.
units.literal: When Gao Yan died, Songnian galloped by post relay to Ye to proclaim the testament; as he spoke, tears streamed down, yet from the start of the proclamation to its end his bearing did not change and his words kept their rhythm.

units.zh: 宣訖，號慟自絕於地，百官莫不感慟。
units.en: When the reading ended he collapsed wailing; every official was moved.
units.literal: When the proclamation ended he wailed and threw himself to the ground; the hundred officials were all deeply moved.

units.zh: 還晉陽，兼侍中，護梓宮還鄴。
units.en: He returned to Jinyang as concurrent palace attendant and escorted the coffin to Ye.
units.literal: He returned to Jinyang, concurrently Palace Attendant, and escorted the coffin back to Ye.

units.zh: 諸舊臣避形跡，無敢盡哀，唯松年哭甚流涕，朝士咸恐。
units.en: Former ministers held themselves in check and none dared mourn openly; only Songnian wept freely, and courtiers were uneasy.
units.literal: The old ministers restrained their bearing; none dared show full grief—only Songnian wept with streaming tears, and the courtiers were all afraid.

units.zh: 武成雖忿松年戀舊情切，亦雅重之。
units.en: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's loyalty to the late emperor, he still respected him.
units.literal: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's deep attachment to the old reign, he also held him in high esteem.

units.zh: 以本官加散騎常侍，食高邑縣幹，參定律令，前後大事多委焉。
units.en: He was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with the salary of Gaoyi county, helped compile laws and statutes, and was entrusted with one major affair after another.
units.literal: In his regular post he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, granted the salary of Gaoyi county, and took part in compiling laws and statutes; major affairs before and after were largely entrusted to him.

units.zh: 兼御史中丞。
units.en: He also served as imperial censor.
units.literal: He concurrently served as Imperial Censor.

units.zh: 發晉陽之鄴，在道遇疾卒。
units.en: Leaving Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.
units.literal: Setting out from Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.

units.zh: 贈吏部尚書、幷州刺史，諡曰平。
units.en: He was posthumously made minister of personnel and inspector of Bing province, with the posthumous name Ping.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and inspector of Bing province; his posthumous title was Ping.

units.zh: 第三子卲，最知名。
units.en: The third son, Shao, was the most famous.
units.literal: The third son Shao was the most renowned.

units.zh: 劉禕，字彥英，彭城人。
units.en: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was from Pengcheng.
units.literal: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was a man of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 父世明，魏兗州刺史。
units.en: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.
units.literal: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.

units.zh: 禕性弘裕，有威重，容止可觀，雖昵友密交，朝夕遊處，莫不加敬。
units.en: Yi was magnanimous and dignified, with a bearing men admired; even close friends who spent every day with him treated him with respect.
units.literal: Yi's nature was broad and generous; he had weight and dignity; his bearing was admirable. Though intimate friends kept close company day and night, none failed to treat him with respect.

units.zh: 好學，善《三禮》，吉凶儀制，尤所留心。
units.en: He loved learning and excelled in the Three Rites, especially the ceremonies of fortune and mourning.
units.literal: He loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; rites of fortune and calamity especially held his attention.

units.zh: 魏孝昌中，釋巾太學博士。
units.en: In the Wei Xiaochang era he entered the academy as erudite.
units.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei he doffed his headcloth and became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 累遷睢州刺史，邊人服其威信，甚得疆埸之和。
units.en: He rose to inspector of Sui province; frontier people trusted his authority and the border was at peace.
units.literal: He rose through posts to inspector of Sui province; the frontier people submitted to his prestige and trust, and the borderlands knew great peace.

units.zh: 世宗輔政，降書褒獎，云：「以卿家世忠純，奕代冠冕，賢弟賢子，並與吾共事，懷抱相托，亦自依然。
units.en: When Gao Cheng was regent he sent a letter of praise, saying, "Your house has been loyal for generations and worn court rank for ages; worthy brothers and sons serve at my side, and the trust between us is unchanged.
units.literal: When Gao Cheng held the regency he sent a letter of commendation, saying, "With your family's generations of loyal purity and successive generations in caps and coronets, worthy younger brothers and worthy sons all serve with me—hearts entrusted to one another, still as before.

units.zh: 宜勗心力，以副所委，莫慮不富貴。」
units.en: Exert yourself to fulfill what I entrust to you; do not doubt that honor and wealth will follow."
units.literal: You should exert your mind and strength to answer what is entrusted—do not worry that wealth and rank will not come."

units.zh: 秩滿，逕歸鄉里侍父疾，竟不入朝。
units.en: When his term ended he went home to tend his father's illness and never returned to court.
units.literal: When his term ended he went straight home to nurse his father's illness and never entered court.

units.zh: 父喪，沉頓累年，非杖不起。
units.en: After his father's death he lay prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.
units.literal: On his father's death he was prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.

units.zh: 世宗致辟，禕稱疾不動。
units.en: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and refused to come.
units.literal: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and would not go.

units.zh: 五子，璇、玘、璞、瑗、瓚，並有志節，為世所稱。
units.en: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had moral resolve and were praised in their time.
units.literal: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had resolve and principle and were praised by the age.

units.zh: 與兄卬廬于墓次，負土成墳。
units.en: He and his elder brother Ang lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb, carrying earth by hand to raise the burial mound.
units.literal: With his elder brother Ang he dwelt in a hut by the grave and carried earth to build the mound.

units.zh: 兄卬當襲父始平侯，以彥師昆弟中最幼，表讓封焉。
units.en: His brother Ang was due to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest brother, Ang petitioned to yield the fief to him.
units.literal: His brother Ang was to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest among the brothers, Ang submitted a memorial offering him the fief.

units.zh: 齊文宣聞而嘉歎，旌表其閭，號其所住為孝終裡。
units.en: When Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard of this he expressed his admiration, erected an honorific marker at his lane, and named his neighborhood Filial Mourning Lane.
units.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard and praised him, marked out his lane with an honorific tablet, and named his dwelling-place Filial Mourning Lane.

units.zh: 時稱友悌孝義，總萃一門。
units.en: The age praised their brotherly devotion and filial righteousness, virtues that seemed to concentrate in a single family.
units.literal: At the time they were praised for brotherly affection and filial righteousness, all gathered in one household.

units.zh: 父同，魏殿中尚書。
units.en: His father Tong had been palace attendant master of writing under the Wei.
units.literal: His father Tong was Wei Palace Attendant Master of Writing.

units.zh: 及輿駕在晉陽，武成鎮鄴，望氣者云鄴城有天子氣。
units.en: When the emperor was at Jinyang and Wucheng (Gao Zhan) held Ye, geomancers declared that Ye possessed the aura of imperial destiny.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Jinyang and Wucheng was stationed at Ye, practitioners of qi-reading said Ye city had the aura of a Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 長廣王湛為大司馬、錄幷省尚書事，解京畿大都督。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang was appointed grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration, and was relieved of the capital-region command.
units.literal: Prince Zhan of Changguang was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province, and was relieved as metropolitan commander of the capital region.

units.zh: 戊子，以太傅、長廣王湛為右丞相，以太尉、平陽王淹為太傅，以尚書令、彭城王浟為大司馬。
units.en: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand tutor, became right chancellor; Prince Yan of Pingyang, then grand commandant, became grand tutor; and Prince You of Pengcheng, director of the Masters of Writing, became grand marshal.
units.literal: On wuzi, the Grand Tutor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was appointed Right Chancellor; the Grand Commandant, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was appointed Grand Tutor; and the Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince You of Pengcheng, was appointed Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統，手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」
units.en: He dispatched envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed him, writing in his own hand: "See that my wife and children are placed somewhere safe; do not do as those before you did."
units.literal: He sent envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed to the great succession, writing in his own hand: "You should place my wife and children in a good place; do not imitate those before you."

units.zh: 帝時以尊親而見猜斥，乃與長廣王期獵，謀之於野。
units.en: Because his rank and kinship made him suspect, Xiaozhao was being pushed aside. He therefore arranged a hunt with Prince Zhan of Changguang and plotted with him in the field.
units.literal: The emperor at that time, because he was an honored kinsman, was regarded with suspicion and pushed aside; he therefore arranged to hunt with the Prince of Changguang and plotted with him in the countryside.

units.zh: 韶與行臺辛術等議，且為受盟。
units.en: Shao discussed with the mobile commissioner Xin Shu and others and provisionally accepted the alliance.
units.literal: Shao discussed with the mobile commissioner Xin Shu and others and provisionally accepted the alliance.

units.zh: 六月，韶遣辯士喻白額禍福，白額於是開門請盟。
units.en: In the sixth month, Shao sent eloquent envoys to explain fortune and disaster to Baie; Baie thereupon opened the gates and requested an alliance.
units.literal: In the sixth month, Shao sent eloquent envoys to explain fortune and disaster to Baie; Baie thereupon opened the gates and requested an alliance.

units.zh: 夏四月辛卯，詔兼散騎常侍皇甫亮使於陳。
units.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinmao day, an edict appointed Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Huangfu Liang envoy to Chen.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinmao day, an edict appointed Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Huangfu Liang envoy to Chen.

units.zh: 李諧於廣坐，因稱其父名曰：「卿嗜熊白生否？」
units.en: At a great gathering Li He invoked his father's name and said, "Do you like raw bear's paw?"
units.literal: Li He at a great gathering invoked his father's name and said, "Do you like raw bear's paw?"

units.zh: 諧遽出避之，道逢其甥高德正。
units.en: He fled at once to avoid him. On the road he met his nephew Gao Dezheng.
units.literal: He fled at once to avoid him; on the road he met his nephew Gao Dezheng.

units.zh: 德正曰：「舅顏色何不悅？」
units.en: Dezheng said, "Uncle, why do you look displeased?"
units.literal: Dezheng said, "Uncle, why is your face not pleased?"

units.zh: 及帝將建中宮，高隆之、高德正言漢婦人不可為天下母，宜更擇美配。
units.en: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.
units.literal: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.

units.zh: 而德正猶固請廢后而立段昭儀，欲以結勳貴之援，帝竟不從而立后焉。
units.en: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.
units.literal: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.

units.zh: 李渾 子湛 渾弟繪 族子公緒 李璵 弟瑾 族弟曉 鄭述祖 子元德
units.en: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande
units.literal: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande

units.zh: 繪，字敬文。
units.en: Hui, styled Jingwen.
units.literal: Hui, styled Jingwen.

units.zh: 贈南青州刺史，謚曰景。
units.en: He was posthumously made governor of Southern Qingzhou; his posthumous title was Jing.
units.literal: He was posthumously made governor of Southern Qingzhou; his posthumous title was Jing.

units.zh: 齊王蕭寶夤引為主簿記室，專管表檄，待以賓友之禮。
units.en: Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin brought him in as chief clerk and recorder, put him in charge of memorials and proclamations, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend.
units.literal: Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin brought him in as chief clerk and recorder, put him in charge of memorials and proclamations, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend.

units.zh: 天平初，世宗用為丞相司馬。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Cheng employed him as staff officer to the chancellor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Cheng employed him as staff officer to the chancellor.

units.zh: 使還，拜平南將軍、高陽內史。
units.en: On his return he was appointed general who pacifies the south and inner administrator of Gaoyang.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed general who pacifies the south and inner administrator of Gaoyang.

units.zh: 天保初，為司徒右長史。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianbao he was chief clerk on the right of the Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was chief clerk on the right of the Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 武定初，兼常侍，為聘梁使主。
units.en: At the beginning of Wuding he was concurrent regular attendant and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was concurrent regular attendant and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.

units.zh: 時勑侍中西河王、秘書監常景選儒學十人緝撰五禮，繪與太原王乂同掌軍禮。
units.en: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince of Xihe and Secretary Director Chang Jing select ten Confucian scholars to compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.
units.literal: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince Xihe of the Western River, Secretary Director Chang Jing, and ten Confucian scholars compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.

units.zh: 魏靜帝於顯陽殿講《孝經》、《禮記》，繪與從弟騫、裴伯茂、魏收、盧元明等俱為錄議。
units.en: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.
units.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.

units.zh: 素長筆札，尤能傳受，緝綴詞議，簡舉可觀。
units.en: He had long excelled at letters; he was especially able to transmit and receive; in compiling and stitching together discussions, his selections were worth viewing.
units.literal: He had long excelled at letters; he was especially able to transmit and receive; in compiling and stitching together discussions, his selections were worth viewing.

units.zh: 年六歲，便自願入學，家人偶以年俗忌，約而弗許。
units.en: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.
units.literal: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.

units.zh: 伺其伯姊筆牘之間，而輒竊用，未幾遂通《急就章》。
units.en: He watched his elder cousin sister between brush and inkstone and would steal use of them; before long he had mastered the Jijiuzhang.
units.literal: He watched his elder cousin sister between brush and inkstone and would steal use of them; before long he had mastered the Jijiuzhang.

units.zh: 司徒高邕辟為從事中郎，徵至洛。
units.en: Grand Secretary Gao Yong summoned him as attendant gentleman; he was called to Luoyang.
units.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Yong summoned him as attendant gentleman; he was called to Luoyang.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 前後行人，皆通啟求市，繪獨守清尚，梁人重其廉潔。
units.en: Envoys who came before and after all sent letters opening relations and seeking trade; Hui alone kept to purity and loftiness — the men of Liang respected his integrity.
units.literal: Envoys who came before and after all sent letters opening relations and seeking trade; Hui alone kept to purity and loftiness — the men of Liang respected his integrity.

units.zh: 繪質性方重，未嘗趨事權勢，以此久而屈沈。
units.en: Hui's nature was square and weighty; he never hurried to serve the powerful — for this reason he long remained suppressed and obscure.
units.literal: Hui's nature was square and weighty; he never hurried to serve the powerful — for this reason he long remained suppressed and obscure.

units.zh: 繪曰：「今在晉陽，肅遏邊寇。」
units.en: Hui said, "He is now at Jinyang, sternly repelling border raiders."
units.literal: Hui said: "He is now at Jinyang, sternly repelling border raiders."

units.zh: 繪曰：「黑獺遊魂關右，人神厭毒，連歲凶災，百姓懷土。
units.en: Hui said, "Black Badger is a stray spirit in the west, loathed by men and spirits alike; year after year brings fierce calamity and the people yearn for their homeland.
units.literal: Hui said: "Black Badger is a stray spirit in the west, loathed by men and spirits alike; year after year brings fierce calamity and the people yearn for their homeland.

units.zh: 丞相奇略不世，畜銳觀釁，攻昧取亡，勢必不遠。」
units.en: The chancellor's stratagems are unmatched in the age; he gathers sharp blades and watches for an opening — attacking the benighted to take the doomed — victory cannot be far."
units.literal: The chancellor's stratagems are unmatched in the age; he gathers sharp blades and watches for an opening — attacking the benighted to take the doomed — victory cannot be far."

units.zh: 繪答書曰：「鴿有六翮，飛則沖天，麋有四足，走便入海。
units.en: Hui replied in a letter, "The pigeon has six pinions — in flight it pierces the sky; the elk has four legs — in running it soon reaches the sea.
units.literal: Hui replied in a letter: "The pigeon has six pinions — in flight it pierces the sky; the elk has four legs — in running it soon reaches the sea.

units.zh: 下官膚體疏懶，手足遲鈍，不能逐飛追走，遠事佞人。」
units.en: This humble officer's flesh is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies or pursue what runs, and go far to serve a flatterer."
units.literal: This humble officer's flesh is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies or pursue what runs, and go far to serve a flatterer."

units.zh: 是時世宗使暹選司徒長史，暹薦繪，旣而不果，咸謂由此書。
units.en: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.
units.literal: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.

units.zh: 渾與弟繪、緯俱為聘梁使主，湛又為使副，是以趙郡人士，目為四使之門。
units.en: Hun and his brothers Hui and Wei had all been chief envoys on missions to Liang; Zhan again served as deputy envoy — hence men of Zhao commandery called them the Gate of Four Envoys.
units.literal: Hun and his brothers Hui and Wei had all been chief envoys on missions to Liang; Zhan again served as deputy envoy — hence men of Zhao commandery called them the Gate of Four Envoys.

units.zh: 河間邢晏，卽繪舅也，與繪清言，歎其高遠。
units.en: Xing Yan of Hejian — Hui's maternal uncle — conversed in pure talk with Hui and admired his loftiness.
units.literal: Xing Yan of Hejian — Hui's maternal uncle — conversed in pure talk with Hui and admired his loftiness.

units.zh: 梁武帝問繪：「高相今在何處？」
units.en: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Hui, "Where is Chancellor Gao now?"
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Hui: "Where is Chancellor Gao now?"

units.zh: 繪曰：「兄所出雖遠，當共車千秋分一字耳。」
units.en: Hui said, "Though what you issue from is remote, you should share one character with Che Qianqiu."
units.literal: Hui said: "Though what you issue from is remote, you should share one character with Che Qianqiu."

units.zh: 繪欲修檻，遂因鬬死。
units.en: Hui wished to build a cage-trap; the beast thereupon died in a fight.
units.literal: Hui wished to build a cage-trap; the beast thereupon died in a fight.

units.zh: 繪曰：「猛獸因鬥而斃，自是偶然，貪此為功，人將窺我。」
units.en: Hui said, "The fierce beast died fighting — that was mere chance; if I greedily claim it as merit, people will peer into me."
units.literal: Hui said: "The fierce beast died fighting — that was mere chance; if I greedily claim it as merit, people will peer into me."

units.zh: 河間守崔謀恃其弟暹勢，從繪乞麋角鴿羽。
units.en: Administrator of Hejian Cui Mou relied on the power of his younger brother Xian and begged from Hui elk horns and pigeon feathers.
units.literal: Administrator of Hejian Cui Mou relied on the power of his younger brother Xian and begged from Hui elk horns and pigeon feathers.

units.zh: 山提以五月至鄴，楊愔卽召太常卿邢卲、七兵尚書崔㥄悛、度支尚書陸操、詹事王昕、黃門侍郎陽休之、中書侍郎裴讓之等議撰儀注。
units.en: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned director of ceremonies Xing Shao, minister of the seven armies Cui Lingjun, minister of revenue Lu Cao, household mentor Wang Xin, yellow gate attendant Yang Xiuzhi, secretariat gentleman Pei Rangzhi, and others to draft the ritual regulations.
units.literal: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned Director of Ceremonies Xing Shao, Minister of the Seven Armies Cui Lingjun, Minister of Revenue Lu Cao, Household Mentor Wang Xin, Yellow Gate Attendant Yang Xiuzhi, Secretariat Gentleman Pei Rangzhi, and others to deliberate on drafting the ritual regulations.

units.zh: 崔暹，字季倫，博陵安平人，漢尚書寔之後也，世為北州著姓。
units.en: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han minister of works, and for generations a leading house of the northern provinces.
units.literal: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han Minister of Works, and for generations a prominent clan of the northern provinces.
